summary:
NASA's fire satellites are changing. MODIS, on Terra and Aqua, has counted fires from space since 2000, and NASA plans to start shutting it down from late 2026. VIIRS replaces it and sees smaller fires, so for the same burning it counts 2.7 to 7.8 times more detections in the eight countries I tested. Put the two records side by side and the past looks calmer than it was.

One Fire Record joins them into one monthly record per place, from 2000 to today, and tests how far off that join is. A fire team picks a country, or zooms the map to a smaller area, and sees whether the latest month is normal there, which months burn most and which years were worst. Every estimated month shows its likely error, and the whole record downloads as a CSV file.
details:
What it does

One Fire Record turns NASA FIRMS fire detections into one monthly record per place, from November 2000 to October 2026, counted the way VIIRS counts. The 2026 months come from NOAA-20 through the FIRMS API. August to October are near-real-time data, so the page marks them provisional.

On one page you get:

- The answer first: was the latest month normal here? With a plain comparison, like "32% of a normal October".

- This season so far: every fire year as a running total, starting in the place's quietest month so a season over New Year is not cut in two, and what the next three months usually bring.

- A 3D globe of this year's fire detections. Zoomed out they glow; zoomed in, each dot is one satellite pixel. Tap a country to open its record.

- Two more map views. "When it burns" colours each 0.2-degree square by its peak month over 26 years. "Unusual now" compares each 0.5-degree square's newest month with the same month in earlier years.

- The seam: one real fire that Aqua MODIS and Suomi NPP VIIRS saw on the same afternoon, every pixel drawn at its true size. It shows why the old record looks too calm.

- A 25-year line that switches between the joined record and each sensor as counted, with a strip showing which satellite wrote each part.

- A burning calendar of years by months, in joined, MODIS or VIIRS view, with a table of every value.

- The months that burn most and the worst years, with a check of whether the worst year comes from the scaling: Terra alone, unscaled, gives its own ranking.

- Your own area: zoom the map and every chart redraws for that view. The link keeps the place, area and view, so you can send it on.

- Downloads: the monthly record and this year's fires as CSV, the map as a picture, and an RSS feed per place that says each month whether it was normal.

- The main lines in Sinhala and Tamil as well as English.

- A method section with the test results and the limits.

A weekly GitHub Action is built to fetch the newest NOAA-20 months, rebuild and test the record, and republish the page.

How it works

1. A script downloads NASA's FIRMS yearly country files: MODIS Collection 6.1 from 2000, and VIIRS 375 m on Suomi NPP from 2012 and on NOAA-20 from 2018.

2. Both sensors are cleaned the same way: vegetation fires only (type 0), and no low-confidence detections.

3. For 2012 to 2021, when both flew and before the Terra and Aqua orbits drifted, it counts how many VIIRS detections there are for each MODIS one. It does this for each calendar month separately, because the gap changes with the fire season.

4. MODIS-only months are multiplied by those factors. Before July 2002 only Terra flew, so those months use Terra-only factors. From February 2012 the record is VIIRS itself, and after Suomi NPP it continues with NOAA-20, scaled on the years both VIIRS satellites flew.

5. The test: hide one shared year, rebuild it from MODIS alone, compare it with what VIIRS saw, and repeat for every year. Across eight countries on four continents, the average miss on a hidden month was 8 to 19% with monthly factors and 9 to 27% with one fixed factor. On yearly totals the two are close, at 4 to 12%.

6. The page is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no server. The first screen loads one file of about 3 KB per country, and the map data loads only when you reach the map, so it works on a phone with a slow connection.

Why now

FIRMS stopped delivering Suomi NPP data on 2 November 2026, and Terra and Aqua are next. Anyone who compares this season with history is now comparing different instruments. A team that sees three times more detections than in 2008 may be seeing a change of sensor rather than more fire. One Fire Record puts both sensors in the same units and shows how big the error of that step is.

I wanted something a fire officer can open on a phone and trust, with a method simple enough to check by hand. Next: every country through the FIRMS API, each new month as it arrives, NOAA-21, and day and night counted apart.

Limits

A scaled month is an estimate with a measured range. Terra-only months are the weakest part of the record. MODIS after 2022 has drifted, so it is not used to learn the factors. A detection is not a fire and not a burned area. A small area uses its whole country's factors.

Tools

Python 3 (standard library only) for the data, HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the page, MapLibre GL JS for the globe, Sentinel-2 cloudless tiles by EOX for the map, Natural Earth for country borders, GitHub Pages for hosting and GitHub Actions for the weekly update.
